summary.title: Writing Helpful Error Messages | Technical Writing | Google for Developers
summary.one_liner: Learn to write and review error messages that clearly state what went wrong and how the user can fix it.
keywords: what went wrong and how to fix it
error messages in ides and command lines
takeaways: A good error message concisely answers two questions: what went wrong, and how the user fixes it.
Common problems with bad error messages include being unactionable, vague, imprecise, confusing, inaccurate, unclear in cause, and lacking next steps.
Good error messages improve user experience, enable self-help, and reduce support workload.
The course covers writing and reviewing error messages, not the code that displays them in a GUI.
summary.summary: This self-study course from Google for Developers teaches how to write and review clear error messages, mainly for developer-facing scenarios such as IDEs, command lines, and GUIs. It is aimed at engineers, program managers, and technical writers, and it recommends first taking Technical Writing One. The page explains why bad error messages frustrate users and lists the benefits of good ones, such as actionability and faster issue resolution. It explicitly excludes the mechanics of generating or displaying error messages.
